utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On Friday, we discussed a document. It was a receipt, if I'm not mistaken. Now I would like to discuss some other matters with you, some other documents. D6/4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Did you say D6/4?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. It should be some kind of receipt. On the name of Antic Ratif. Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Mr. Ninkovic, what your copy is like but could you please try to have a look at it and see what it's all about? Can you tell us something about this document? Actually, tell me first, can you tell me the name?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Antic Ratif.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What's this receipt all about?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, this receipt has to do with military materiel, pistol, ammunition, 9 millimetres, 5.000 pieces. Then ammunition for an automatic rifle, 7.62, and finally hand grenade, M-75. So all of this comes from the arsenal of the Yugoslav People's Army, as for the origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the quantities here, but it's not necessary for me to read them out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. There is no need to do that. So the date up there is March, 1992, all right. Well that's not contested?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Usher could we now have exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Could we have the document for a short while on the ELMO in order to refresh one's mind? Okay, that's enough for me, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit D20/4, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put it on the ELMO, Mr. Ninkovic, and could you look at it from there so that the rest of us could also follow it? Tell me, you've already commented upon a similar receipt. Just tell me what is this 04 plus 1 and M160, these two abbreviations?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are clips for automatic rifles. They are packed as 4 plus 1. That is to say for automatic rifles, they are packed in 4 plus 1 clip packages and then the bullets are M160.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know the person who allegedly received this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One more question: This number up here, 1397B, what does that mean? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be the number of the rifle concerned or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What do you know about this person, is this person from Samac, the one who received this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You don't know what ethnicity this person was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know. A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know this person's party affiliation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit D25/4? What I'm interested in, according to my specification, Exhibit D25/4 is a 12-pages long document, but I see that it's only 3, but the fact is that first three pages are ID, so maybe that's kind of -- in fact, according to the specification that I have in front of me, is -- yeah. This is the rest of the document, yes. Because we have to discuss this document in totality, no matter whether the first three pages are remaining ID at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take a look at this. Mr. Ninkovic, take a look at it, the last three pages should be the first three actually according to the real order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. Can I have a look, please? Yes. Could we have the three remaining pages, please? That's correct, yes. Now it should be complete like this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Pantelic, please. The interpreters cannot hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, your mike.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. [Interpretation] Could you please put this on the ELMO? [In English] Well, to be sure, Your Honour, because I believe that some of these documents are under seal, some part of these documents, which are not so sure here which one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is there any under seal? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Except for attachment 1, 2, 3 which remained ID the whole document is an exhibit and is not under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's proceed with -- we waste so much time on this getting started.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, what would your comment be with regard to this document? First of all, have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it with Mr. Milosevic [As interpreted] the inspector, federal inspector at the public security station in Samac. May I comments upon this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a second, please, here. It says federal inspector, Mr. Milosevic. Line 23, and 24. We have some problems with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Line 23 and 24, he said actually Mr. Milos Savic, not Mr. Milosevic. And he didn't say it was a federal inspector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you just repeat that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly request the witness to speak in a different way. It is very hard to discern what he is saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw this document with Mr. Milos Savic, crime prevention inspector, who worked at the public security station in Samac. When we had that document on Friday, the block scheme, I gave my comment. I see here an elaboration in detail of this block schematic, which fully develops the formation structure of the armed formation of a paramilitary nature consisting of Muslims, under the leadership of the Party of Democratic Action. So we have a detailed list of lower level units, engineering, anti-sabotage, reconnaissance, observation, and other units, and also a list of members of these lower level units. So this is a classical list of members of a military formation. This document constitutes an organisational formation structure of a particular unit, and this can be seen from the actual title.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have now Exhibit D26/4, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, there is just a matter I wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Di Fazio, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I thought I had it on. Ah, it's come on now, I believe. Can the Chamber hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Sorry. If Your Honours please, the last three documents that we've had examination-in-chief on, have revealed nothing to us that you couldn't discern from the face of the document and particularly so in the last question. I am going to object to any further examination-in-chief that is simply a recital of what is plain and obvious from the face of the document. There is two reasons for that. The first reason is that it's not relevant and it cannot assist you what you can read from the document, or you can read from the document and draw your own conclusions. The second reason is, if Your Honours please, that I had unfortunately made a mistake in thinking that we were going to be sitting until Wednesday. I thought it was for some reason it was my mistake that we were sitting until Wednesday, the 11th. I'm informed that in fact we only have a half day tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to be able to finish and I'm sure the Chamber would like to see me finish my cross-examination of this witness. If we are going to spend a good part of the morning going through documents and reading out what's on the face of them, time is being wasted and my cross-examination opportunities are going to be eroded and eroded significantly. So I suggest that Mr. Pantelic not lead further evidence on documents if it's only going to be telling us, restating what you can read from the document itself. If there is a special insight, I've got no problem at all, and welcome the witness' evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, this is the Defence case. The position of the Defence is that we have here in fact only one witness, I'm speaking of the Defence of Blagoje Simic, who can, with his professional background, tell us in fact the nature -- explain us the nature of these various documents. I cannot have comments on these documents from a member of executive board or a physician or some other person. So this is absolutely suitable from the point of view of the Defence, that this witness could give us a comment. On the other hand, this witness is a fact witness because he is a citizen of Samac and he knows certain persons who appear to be on various documents, including the last one and all other previous ones. And also, he can also give us certain, I would say, personal point of personal knowledge of the background of certain events in Samac which might be relevant for this case. And secondly -- or thirdly, Your Honour, the Defence gave to this Trial Chamber an estimated time of various witnesses. For this particular witness, our estimation was around ten hours. I don't believe, and I really, to be honest, Your Honour, it's not a matter for the Defence to speed up things for the interests of the Prosecution. The Prosecution could be very relaxed, they have enough time, they will have enough time to give their cross-examinations, whether today or tomorrow or the day after tomorrow I mean in the next session. Let me remind you, respectfully remind you, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, can you -- no, no, no, can you listen?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have the right to go on with your Defence as you have planned it, but the Trial Chamber will direct you when you're going wrong and the point Mr. Di Fazio made of simply reciting what is on the document, that is not necessary because when the document is admitted as an exhibit, the contents are on record. So avoid that and lead your witness to evidence which you afford a defence to your client, not just describing events if he was not there, then it doesn't help.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will take care about that, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And even if the time, as you say, was estimated, the Trial Chamber can cut it down once we notice that you are simply wasting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will stick on that, Your Honour, thank you. Okay, could we have now Exhibit D26/4, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I make a comment in relation to the previous matters we discussed? In terms of the link between the document that was the block schematic and this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, you can go ahead. Excuse me, let's just clarify one thing, the block schematic is the document that you commented upon on Friday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two closely interlinked planning documents that are customary in military planning. The first document is simpler and it's easier do have an overview from it, whereas the second one is an elaboration, which includes the manning of that unit with specific personnel. When such a document is compiled, there are all the necessary prerequisites for it to become executed. Now, what does that mean? That means that that unit, that military unit, in this case it's a paramilitary unit, is prepared to carry out the task that is ordered to do, because it has a fully developed structure, internal structure, and it has a system of command. Without such a structure, there can be no command over units. So along with the mobilisation document that we saw on Friday, this is a fully completed structure of units of paramilitary nature in Samac, consisting of Muslims. So we have weapons, we have a unit, we have a mobilisation plan, and the only remaining thing is to put a task before them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one is that now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is D26/4, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once you've had a look at it, would you please place it on the ELMO? Page 2 of this document, actually. And when you compare it to page 3, I would be interested in hearing what you conclude on the basis of that. First of all, tell me, have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. We see names we know here, Sulejman Tihic, Alija Fitozovic, et cetera, but from an operational point of view, when you look at the previous page, I would be interested in hearing your comment: How can the President of the SDA be commander of a unit? Is that customary practice? So what did this actually look like in practice, in doctrine, too?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about doctrine and commanding the troops, the customary solution is that the head of state is Commander-in-Chief, and that he issues all orders to the general staff of the army. That is the customary solution. Any interference of political parties constitutes an attack on the existing order of a country in the most flagrant terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Ninkovic, the translation is using the word "doctrine." I presume from your comment that you mean the usual theory, when you say "doctrine." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We can put it that way, that it's theory. But we can talk about the application of this theory in actual pieces of legislation, in laws, especially the law on defence and the law on army. This is an obligation. This is the system of command and control.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Pantelic, please. The interpreters cannot hear him at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, your microphone is off. Can you repeat what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please look at page 3, Mr. Ninkovic and tell us which persons do you know from this particular schematic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally know Mr. Sulejman Tihic. He was president of the Party of Democratic Action, as he is today. Alija Fitozovic went to school with me. I know him from school. But he was older than me. He was the most exposed member of the Muslim units in their organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, again, translation. Mr. Fitozovic was, "The most exposed member of the Muslim units." That's line 24. Could we have an explanation on what that means from Mr. Ninkovic, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not use that word. I said the most exposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: No. Exactly, but what do you mean by "the most exposed member"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In what sense? Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not utter that word. I am talking about [Microphone not activated] who had the most influence in setting up these units. I exclude Mr. Tihic. That is to say, a person who was in charge of organising paramilitary units in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you still know the names? Do you know the names below?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the messengers: Kurtic Galib; Vukovic Ahmet; Hadzialijagic Suad; not all of them, but I know some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where are they from?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now tell me, please, what we see here below, how do you interpret this word "park" what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the call-up point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And where is it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in Samac. I mean the call-up point is the place where people gather, where called-up unit members gather. That is, they meet there and then they go out to perform their tasks. This is where the number of those who had responded, who have responded to the call-up is checked and then this unit is used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now we have a number of documents, which the Defence intends to tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact the Trial Chamber can find it on -- the first document under the internal number R-1. So this is the letter signed by commander, Mr. Obradovic, from -- I don't know. It's kind of commander, military unit, letter signed to TO of Bosanski Samac. The date is -- should be April, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please put it on the ELMO so that everybody will see it? This is obviously 1991. I can see the date and everything, but can you comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm familiar with this document. That is, I saw it in the office where I worked. I'm also familiar with the undersigned, with the commander, so this is the execution of the order of the Presidency of the SFRY, ordering to disband all units which are not integrated in the armed forces of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. That is, which orders to hand over these -- their weapons and transfer them to the barracks in Derventa. I know that that was done in several municipalities of the region, in Bosanski Brod, Odzak, Samac, Orasje, Modrica, Gradacac. There was a depot in Derventa for these weapons and this is that barracks which is mentioned here, in Derventa. I also know that this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection, if Your Honours, please. However, that is not to be seen as any acceptance of authenticity or anything like that on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D121/1 and D121/1 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is R9. It's an order dated 6 of May, 1992, signed by the -- Mr. Odobasic, coordinator of 1st Derventa Brigade, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell us, Mr. Ninkovic, what is this document, as to its form?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concretely, it is an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But is it in line with the usual form of orders?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the upper corner, it says which armed formation this is. Have you heard of it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the Republic of Croatia. As far as I know, these are the armed formations of the Republic of Croatia, which were on the front in Bosanska Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean did you see this document before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it when I was preparing with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to tender these documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. If Your Honours please, I object to that. There is absolutely no evidence to indicate the relevance of this document to these proceedings. If Mr. Pantelic can elicit some evidence from the witness showing why we are looking at this document, what the purpose of it is, how it helps him, what point in the Defence it goes to, then perhaps I might withdraw my objection, but at the moment, it's an incomprehensible military document from Croatia. How is it relevant to us? If we had that explanation, I might withdraw my objection, but at the moment I can't understand the point and the purpose of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: First of all, it is obvious that the document was issued by the Croatian army with headquarters in Slavonski Brod which is the territory of Croatia. However, it was sent to 1st Bosnian Brod Brigade, which is a brigade under the command of commander Mr. Bilic, which is in fact HVO Brigade in Bosnia, not in Croatia. And furthermore, under the point number 1, we could find name Sijekovac, which we have quite extensively discussed, that place where the massacre against Serbs were committed by the elements of HVO and Croatian army. This document is -- from the point of view of the Defence, this document will be discussed with the other military witness which will come, I believe, during the -- Mr. Zaric case. I don't have any problem now to have it by -- under the ID, but the relevance to our case is that Defence would like to show that the broader context of the conflict in Samac area, Odzak area, was initiated by the members of a foreign army, which in this case is Croatian army in connection with the elements of the HVO army in Croatian community Bosanska Posavina, as well as with the elements of their Crisis Staff in Samac, HDZ. So totality we think that this document is of great importance for our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, it will be admitted. What matters is how much weight the Trial Chamber will afford it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D122/1 and D122/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next document that I would like to discuss with this witness is our internal number is R10. This is the conclusion dated June the 1st, 1992, in Odzak, signed by HVO council president, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, if it's easier for you to see, then you can look on your right-hand side, at the document, not go via screen. First, are you familiar with the institution indicated in the upper left corner of the document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the Croat Defence Council, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, could you -- as a matter of fact, comment on this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croat Defence Council took over the legislation in the military matters from the Republic of Croatia. This means that the system of command in the HVO was compatible with the same system in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have a number for this exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D123/1 and D123/1 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next document is R11. This is kind of letter dated 5th of June, 1992, sent by the coordinator of veterinarian station, to the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is dated the 5th of June, as we can see. At that time, were you not directly at that place, isn't it? That is you were not the head of the department?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But regardless, tell me, is this the usual document sent by companies requesting people for the labour obligation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have a number for this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I have no objection to the admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can make a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can make your comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps while that's being attended to, I just wonder which company it was that called up these workers? It seems to me that it's -- unless it's the veterinarian station is said to be a company. Am I understanding that evidence in that way? Am I correct in understanding this evidence in that way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the witness could explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Clarify, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The veterinary station is an institution which works, and whose chief task is to treat animals in the municipality of Samac. If it is to be able to do that, it needs a number of professionals. That is veterinary doctors, veterinary assistants and other paraveterinary personnel. Without that personnel, the veterinary station cannot do its job. And therefore, the director and the coordinator of that station in Samac asks for -- requests to be sent persons who are on the list. At that time, there was a particular problem involving a large number of heads of cattle, a lot of livestock. There was nobody to look after this livestock and that is an additional reason for making this request.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honours, might like to know why it was sent to the, as I read the document, why it was sent to the Crisis Staff and not the Ministry of Defence, who is handing out work tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, is that for this -- the witness wouldn't be able to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because he's not the originator.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If these people are performing work obligation of some sort, maybe that that's what they are doing, then the witness has given extensive evidence about how that was organised by the Ministry of Defence. This seems to me to be going to the Crisis Staff and so therefore the Chamber might be interested to know why is it that the Crisis Staff is involving itself directly in the obligation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's a matter for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- and not the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe it's a matter for cross-examination to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well, I'll withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Otherwise we are losing the sense of the examination-in-chief. Yes. So do we have a number for this document, the previous one? Ah, yes, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be exhibits D124/1 and D124/1 ter, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very good, thank you. Could we have now our internal number, document under R12 dated 5th of June, 1992, sent by the director, manager of company Tekstilac to executive board, Serbian municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Ninkovic, look at this. Take a look. It is a two page document. Perhaps we shall be able to help our learned friend with this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see the date is the same as on the previous document, is isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, 5th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this document, R12, is its number, and it is addressed to the executive board. Now, how do you explain it that the other document was sent on the same day by two different companies, one to the executive board and the other one to the staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I think that the coordinator of the veterinary station was not sufficiently well informed about the matters concerning the economy and labour, and he therefore addressed his letter to the wrong address. This one is sent to the right address, that is the executive committee of the municipality of Samac and it is the manager's request to engage a number of workers pursuant to labour obligation, as you can see this is a request based on qualification in the first place; that is, they are textile workers of different profiles. We see here in the list workers coming from all three working groups, so the chief reason behind this is to have high quality labour so that they could perform the jobs facing that company. So this is the usual document and the procedure which existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ninkovic, in the translation, page 19, line 1, it says "that the list workers come from all three working groups." Is that what in fact you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, I heard -- that was just my intention to clarify the transcript. He said absolutely different thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned that all these workers came from three groups. What group did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ethnic communities. That is Muslims, Serbs and Croats. The director was motivated by the need to have adequate labour and he formulated his request on the basis of the required qualifications, skills, that he needed, and that is how these names on the list came to be on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have an exhibit number for this document, Your Honour? Madam Registrar, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D125/1 and D125/1 ter, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next document that I would like to discuss with this witness is our internal number R13. This is the decree published in Official Gazette number 9, on 13th of June, 1992. It's a decree on the disposition of all material resources for the needs of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is self-explanatory. However, what I'd like to know is get some comments from you. Tell me, when your department of the Ministry of Defence, that is the municipal department, isn't it, in Samac, did you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Pose certain number of questions. You can sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in the course of your work, did you and your associates come across this government decree?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But briefly, and only professionally, will you please explain to us what was the purpose behind, what was the intention behind, this decree and how did it -- how was it enforced in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony so far, I've pointed out that physical and legal entities are also under the obligation to make contributions for the defence. So this position is elaborated on here and the document was issued by the government on the basis of the authority that the government had. So physical and legal persons are duty-bound to, when so requested by the Ministry of Defence, provide some material resource which is on the list to meet the needs of the army. Now, how did this work? Well, an army unit applies to the Ministry of Defence requesting that an asset be requisitioned for that unit, say a tractor. On the basis of the official records in the Ministry of Defence department, and it exists, in the following manner, or every registered tractor in the public security station, that is in the police station, is also entered in the records of the Ministry of Defence on a special card. Then the Ministry of -- the department of the Ministry of Defence receives this request for -- to requisition this. They analyse the tractor records, that is check whether there is such a tractor as is being applied for, and then the department calls the owner of that tractor and tells him to place his tractor at the army's disposal. He is issued then with a document which is called the disposition on the requisitioning and the law and the decree are indicated there, that is the specific article, paragraph and so on and so forth. The document is issued in three copies, one goes to the owner, one to the unit, and one stays in the archives of the department of the Ministry of Defence. This -- the unit is also issued with a form of a military driving licence called the -- the abbreviation of which is PMS-10 where the technical data for the tractor are entered, that is the chassis number, the make, the year of manufacture and so on and so forth. And then this resource is placed at the disposal of the army as long as it may need it. So this is the procedure applied when material resources are requisitioned.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please switch on his microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have no microphone on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Article 1, Mr. Ninkovic, in Article 1 in this decree I see a circle of people -- sorry, a circle of entities, beneficiaries of these resources and among other things, it says here that citizens are also under the same obligation and institutions and companies and other legal persons, and they say for the state administration, economy, and non-production activities. Right. We understand this category and army and everything, that is army-related, but what did this specifically mean? Who could be other beneficiaries in wartime?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to the army a request to requisition a particular material resource, could also be made by the police, civil defence structures, companies, administrative agencies, say the Municipal Assembly of Samac or one of its departments, that is the cadastre or say, the revenue department, or, for instance, a health centre or hospital, a school. In other words, any legal person which can justify its need to be given a requisition material resource.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were talking about the agricultural machinery. That is what I'm interested in, but not in item 1. Item 1 of the same article includes passenger vehicles of all types, in Samac, were there any such instances when private vehicles were -- passenger vehicles were requisitioned?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this embrace all citizens of Samac regardless of their ethnicity or was there any difference?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All citizens of the municipality of Samac who owned the material resources indicated in the decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. But under 21, this decree says that it also applies to livestock, as the -- it is an agricultural area and that livestock is pretty important. Will you tell me something about that? Were there some -- was there any implementation of this decree taking place?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One could requisition draft animals, horses as a rule, for the army or some other structures, but mostly were motor vehicles which could not pass, that is, where there were no possible roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. I'd like to hear your comment about this paragraph. I believe it is paragraph 3 of the article. "Below item 24, it says that apart from the resources in paragraph 1 of the decree, the citizens are also bound to hand over their weapons." Will you please explain it to me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be on the ELMO because the interpreters have not been given any copies of these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the item. I didn't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Below item 24, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The citizens are also bound to hand over their weapons. How was this enforced? What was the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see the public security station, the Ministry of the Interior, in peace time, keeps the record of owners of weapons, that is pistols, hunting rifles, carbines and other weapons as permitted by law. If a citizen has a weapon of this kind, and there is a need for it, then he is duty-bound to hand it over. However, the department of Ministry of Defence did not conduct that procedure. That is hunting, personal and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, on page 2 of this decree, the way in which resources are taken, et cetera, is elaborated upon. Were there any records kept of these resources that were requisitioned?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, allow me to explain. In a military unit, there is a service which is called the personnel service. That is where records are kept on the personnel of the unit concerned and also records about resources that were mobilised, requisitioned, that is to say, vehicles, tractors, livestock, horses, vessels, perhaps, et cetera. Also, there are records at the Department of Defence about the requisitioned and mobilised resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I assume --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I can deal with this document with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say something else here. It is well known in other legal systems as well that there is this legal provision for giving material resources for defence needs. I'm going to quote an example from recent history. When Argentina attack the Falkland Islands then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We don't need that history.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, this is a criminal trial and there are specific charges against the accused persons and the Defence have to answer those specific charges. So there is no need to give any evidence touching other countries, touching history.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, as for using these resources, the owners were compensated for that, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was this compensation paid to the actual owners of the property requisitioned? Tell us how was this done, because after all, if somebody takes somebody's car, what are the rights of the owner of that car in terms of compensation and how was this regulated in practice? Actually, we are talking about Samac, just Samac.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The owner of the car concerned has the right to compensation. He has the right to indemnification as well if there was any damage incurred during the use of that particular property, in this case a car. If the resource concerned was requisitioned for the army, then it was the army or rather the Republika Srpska that was duty-bound to meet that obligation. However, if the particular material resource was requisitioned for the use of a particular company, of the municipality, of the medical centre, the hospital, et cetera, then it is the said institution that is duty-bound to indemnify the person for the damage incurred on the resource concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Damage is one thing and compensation for regular use is another thing. I assume that you are referring to indemnification and to compensation as things that have to be paid by the user of the particular resource; right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In Samac, was this procedure observed? I'm talking about 1992 and 1993. Do you know anything about the situation today, from the point of view of these processes, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, as far as I know, there weren't any resources for paying such damages. So this remained as war damages that the government of Republika Srpska is supposed to pay for. After the war, there were many proceedings going on in this respect. The government also had sessions devoted to this because the percentage of war damage is very high and there are court proceedings that had been instituted too. It was published in the Official Gazette and I'm aware of this, because this is a public publication, that legal and physical persons won their particular cases before courts of law. And that the Court of law, according to its judgement, practically automatically takes the amount concerned from the bank account of the Ministry of Defence and the amount is the one that corresponds to that mentioned in the decision of the relevant court. So this also referred to the budget of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 14 of this decree, Mr. Ninkovic, speaks about the deadlines for making these payments, and if not -- I mean when you gave this explanation now did you actually bear in mind Article 14?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 9 talks about the use of housing property and other buildings for defence needs. Were there such cases as well? We were talking about moveable property so far, and we know that buildings and the like are immovable property. Was that also the case in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, in the territory of the municipality of Samac, at the front line which was on the north and the south, there were quite a few units of the Army of Republika Srpska. I'm just going to mention a few of them so that you can get more insight as far as the number of personnel was concerned, and also the needs for engaging housing property for these purposes. On the southern front line, there was the Sana Brigade [As interpreted] and other big brigades of several thousand persons, then parts of the 2nd Posavina Brigade and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The transcript isn't accurate. I believe it's line 24, on page 26, first Brigade, if I remember correctly, was Prijedor Brigade and I don't see this in the transcript. Then after this Brigade, he was talking about Sanska Brigade. And this is not what I see here in the transcript. Line 24 and 25 on page 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, we really don't have to go into all these details. If I understood you correctly, there were a lot of troops there. How many soldiers of Republika Srpska were in that zone, put it that way?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 15.000 and 20.000 soldiers. So these units addressed themselves to the defence department in the territory of the municipality so that they would mobilise housing facilities in the territory of the municipality for their purposes, so these are apartment buildings, family houses, parts of company buildings, et cetera, and that is what we did as part of regular procedure. And a very large number of such facilities were mobilised, especially outside Samac, in the field, rather within the villages in the zone of the front line, for putting up the headquarters of various units and also units attached to the staff for soldiers themselves, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ninkovic, concerning the apartment buildings and family houses, were these vacant properties and if they were not vacant properties, what happened to the families who were living in those apartments and houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the most part, we mobilised -- well, if we are talking about the mobilisation of houses, we mobilised -- we mobilised houses, mostly those that belonged to Serbs because these villages in the zone along the front line, for the most part, belonged to people who were abroad or perhaps if they were at home, then the area would be used in the following way: For example, if there were two facilities within a single court yard, then one would be used for the needs of the military and the other one would be used for putting up the family that lives there any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more explanation, Mr. Ninkovic. When you referred to the number of 15 to 20.000 soldiers, in which period was this? Can you give us a more specific period?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the department of the Ministry of Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just give me the time.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we talk about the work of the department of the Ministry of Defence, we are talking about the end of 1992 and during the war. That is to say the entire course of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In Article 8 of this decree, it says that the tariff shall be stipulated by the Ministry of Finance. This is the tariff that is compensation for the use of such property. Did you apply this tariff as prescribed by the Ministry of Finance or did you in the municipality of Samac have any special tariffs for compensating for the use of such resources?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not within the province of work of the department of Ministry of Defence. This had to do with the Ministry of Finance and I did not have any contact with this, nor did I have any experience with this kind of thing in my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could we have a number for this exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D126/1 and D126/1 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document that I would like to discuss with this witness is our internal number is R18. Well, it's in fact, I believe it's Prosecution document -- I mean not by origin, they delivered us. It's ERN number 00841532. This is an order dated 19th of July, 1992, order signed by the General Momir Talic, regarding the introduction of military administration in municipality of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take a look at this document, Mr. Ninkovic, and tell me the following. First of all, are you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Usher, please I will discuss this document for some time, so you can take your seat. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Ninkovic, tell us about the circumstances, when and how did you find out about this document, and what was done in accordance with this document? Well, there, that would be the explanation we require.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of July, 1992. Colonel Gojko Vujinovic came, from the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps, and he held a brief meeting with the representatives of the municipality of Samac. As far as I can remember, it was at the heating plant; that is the locality where the meeting was held. He briefly familiarised the persons present with this order and the reason why he came was that he requested from the leadership of the municipality of Samac to help restore the public utilities in Samac, that is to say, water works, the power supply, and other vital services.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, one second I have to intervene at this moment, because it's here on the page 30, line 8, he said "To restore the public utilities in Odzak." That's what he said because there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I was wondering why it should be Samac. Actually. Can we have a correction?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just clarify this. When you said that these public utilities should be reconstructed, what municipality did you mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall repeat. Colonel Gojko Vujinovic came to visit the leadership of the municipality of Samac and he asked the leadership for the municipality of Samac to help Odzak in revitalising the vital public utilities, that is to say, the water supply system, the power supply system, the sewage system, and other services that are indispensable for the life of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, who was head of this military administration?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean who was the person in person who was head of the military administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you who the commander was.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were two persons that rotated. I know Colonel Radomir Simic. I just don't know whether he was the first or the second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. This area of responsibility, we are talking about the municipality of Odzak, is within which military unit, higher level unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the command of the 1st Krajina Corps, Tactical Group 1, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, furthermore, here in this order, reference is made to booty. What is that? What did the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps mean when they mentioned booty? Under item 3 it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honour please, I object to that question, I object strenuously. That is asking this witness for his interpretation of the meaning of the word in a document when it's plain for us to read the word. We know what booty is. We know what the spoils of war are. They are very clear expressions in anybody's language. Now, unless this witness has a particular insight into what the author of the document, Momir Talic, had in mind when the document was created, unless he can directly give you clear, unequivocal evidence, that shows that there was a special meaning to be attached to that particular expression or use of the word, then I object to his interpretation of the meaning of the word in this particular document. It's not evidence that you should hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your personal knowledge, Mr. Ninkovic, in relation to the procedure regarding booty, the spoils of war, collecting that? You are an expert and you were there in the field. What can you tell us about that in the territory of Odzak? How was this operationalised, this part of the order relating to booty, the spoils of war? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot present many details regarding this. I just know that there were persons, there were military personnel in the command of Tactical Group 1 that were in charge of this and that were engaged in such matters. Milan Dukljanin was commander of Tactical Group 1. I personally knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, I'm interested in the following: Item 6, how did the process of settling the territory of the municipality of Odzak function or rather, what persons, of which ethnicity, populated that area? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be said that a fierce battle was waged there between the formations of the Army of Republika Srpska and the Croat Defence Council. That is to say, that this was front line fighting in that battle, in that military battle, the Serb army pushed back the Croatian Defence Council. As far as I know, the Croatian Defence Council previously evacuated its own civilian population of Croat ethnicity. So that territory was -- actually part of the territory of the municipality was not populated. Serbs who were in prison and in detention in Odzak, I mentioned Strolit, the metallurgy plant in Odzak, they were taken to the front line, to Bosanski Brod and Slavonski Brod to detention facilities there. So after this fighting that took place in that part of the municipality of Odzak, I am referring to that part of the territory, so in that part of the territory, not the entire population was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. This was a very short and clear question: Were any Serbs expelled from the territory of the municipality of Odzak and who were temporarily staying in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now I'm asking you what happened to these people when military administration was introduced and when this civilian life was being organised? What happened to people who originally came from the municipality of Odzak and then came to the municipality of Samac? Explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They started coming back slowly, to the area of the municipality of Odzak, and conditions were supposed to be created for their return there, that is to say, drinking water, electricity. Then houses should have been repaired, as much as possible, that is to say, elementary conditions for civilian life.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the process of return of Serb refugees from the territory of the municipality of Odzak, was that an ongoing process in 1992 and 1993? That is to say, people going from Samac to Odzak, was this an ongoing process of these families moving back?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did all these people remain there until the present day? Where are these people?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This process was very slow. In the area of the municipality of Odzak, nowadays, there are hardly any Serbs left. I'm going to say specifically about my village, Donja Dubica, where there were 212 houses with 880 inhabitants. Now, there are only 8 or 9 inhabitants who returned. The rest are in Australia, America, et cetera. Partly in Samac and Modrica, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Why? Why did people not return to their homes? What's the reason? Why didn't they stay on there, why didn't they go on living there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Serb property there was totally destroyed. Houses were razed to the ground, especially Trnjak, Dubica and Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And which entity is Odzak now?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, just if I may assist the Chamber, I've listened to what the witness has said and I think I understand his position, what he's saying, but what's not clear to me from the last passage of evidence, is whether his position is that Article 6 of D127/1 is expressly directed towards Serbs who were living -- who had been living in Odzak, went to Bosanski Samac and then went back and resettled in Odzak. There is nothing in there, of course, that expressly selects them as a class of people, but if the position of the witness is, Article 6 is talking about the displaced Serbs from Odzak, then I think he should make his position clear for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, can that be clarified?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe that we have exhibit number for this document, that's one thing. Another thing, it's 11.00. It's time for our break. Maybe we could deal with that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, let me clear this. Which one did you refer to? You did mention D127/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think the document has been marked prematurely by my case manager. It hasn't yet gone into evidence. When it does, this document will then be D127. My question simply is: Article 6 of this document, which will be an exhibit, does it refer -- is it talking about Odzak Serbs? That's what I think we should know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall take our break and continue the proceedings at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, before the recess, an issue was opened regarding item 6 of this order. I would like to hear your response as to who did the military command administration permit the settling of the territory during the period this administration existed?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The command of the military administration in Odzak approved this to all civilians who expressed the wish to that effect and who wanted to go back to the territory of the Odzak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this apply to specific ethnic communities or was there any other system that was applied in that respect?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This applied to all ethnic communities, and in the territory of the municipalities of Samac and partly Modrica, there were Croats and Muslim refugees as well, apart from Serbs, who expressed a wish to return to Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the last item of this order, we see that the authorities of Modrica, Doboj and Bosanski Samac were supposed to be informed thereon. Are these bordering municipalities of Odzak?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are the neighbouring municipalities of the municipality of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, the civilian authorities in Samac, what kind of attitude did they adopt towards Odzak, the military administration in Odzak? Did the civilian authorities have the power to issue orders to the administration in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What were the obligations of the civilian authorities in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this agreement that had been reached, on the occasion of the visit of Colonel Vujnovic, who was Commander Talic's assistant for civilian affairs within the command of the 1st Krajina Corps, the leadership of the Samac municipality expressed their readiness to assist in the revitalisation of public utilities and other public companies which were necessary in order to create circumstances for the return of civilians. In this respect, the sewage system, the power and water supply system, the PTT company, the veterinarian station, and the health centre, I believe, had certain obligations in that respect, pertaining to their relevant area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please explain to us what obligations did members of the civilian structure have when a decision had to be implemented? Was an approval of the military administration necessary? Could you explain to us how this worked?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to be able to move to the territory which was under the control of the military administration, one had to have a laissez-passer, a kind of movement permit. Once I didn't have such a permit and my identity was checked at the checkpoint and I was taken to the command of the military police where the issue was cleared up and I was finally released, but this is just to tell you that it was not possible to do anything without the approval and the knowledge of the command of the Odzak military administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any contacts between the representatives of the Republika Srpska government and the military administration? Could you elucidate this issue for us a little bit, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the government of Mr. Lukic, that is the second government, the first one was presided by Mr. Jeric, and then sometime in the spring of 1993, the national assembly voted a new government of the Serbian Republic of BH, whose president was Mr. Vladimir Lukic. Now, his government, and I think it was on the proposal of the Defence Minister, examined the case of Odzak, the case of the military administration in Odzak, which did not exactly have a firm base in law. This government therefore, appointed a four-member commission. A lady from the Ministry of Justice was the President of this commission and she was joined by three men. I knew personally Vlado Vukovic from the Defence Ministry. Then there was a gentleman from the Ministry of Agriculture and Water Works and another gentleman from the Ministry of Energetics and Industry. They were sent to the Odzak municipality with the task of examining the facts concerning the military administration and to find out how it functioned. Since the ministry department is a republic organ, a republic body, and since I knew this gentleman, Mr. Vukovic, they came to see me so that I could take them to Odzak. I was, after all, a local resident. I was familiar with the area. And they thought that I was the right person to take them there. Therefore, we visited the area together and we wanted to see the commander of the military administration, Mr. Radomir Simic, who that day was not in his office. There were some lower ranking officers there, with whom we had a conversation, and then the commission in question visited some companies and some institutions and they noted that there were cases of dismantling of facilities of various companies. The gentleman from the Ministry of Industry made some notes and after this visit, we went back to Samac on the same day, and the lady from the Ministry of Justice used my telephone and called the president of the government from my office, Mr. Lukic. She explained to him what she had seen in Odzak. I was present during that telephone conversation. Mr. Lukic, the President of the government, after this conversation, said to the lady that she should wait there, at the telephone, because there was a fax there as well, that he was going to issue a written order. Half an hour later, approximately, a written order indeed arrived. I personally saw it, and I read it. It specified that as of today, that is the date this order was issued, from the territory of the municipality of Odzak, no material resources could be taken away. This was in June, 1993, though I cannot tell you the exact date, but it must have been in June. The commission spent the night in Samac and then on the following day, we went to the command of the Odzak military administration, where we found the commander, Mr. Radomir Simic, who had come from Doboj. He had been in Doboj before that, for reasons of his military capacity. The President of this commission explained to him the reasons of her visit and she also told him what she had seen was going on on the territory of the Odzak municipality. She also told him that she had talked to Mr. Vladimir Lukic, the president of the government, and she showed him this written document and its contents. Colonel Radomir Simic took note of that and a few minutes later, a man appeared at the door, who carried a piece of paper which seemed to be a list of some sorts, and he asked Mr. Simic, "Is this all okay? Has this been agreed upon?" It seems that this was a list containing a number of artifacts, a number of material resources, and Mr. Simic said, "Yes, it's okay." He probably meant that this is in accordance with some sort of previous agreement and that these material resources could be taken away, could be seized. But this lady who was the president of the commission and who was from the Ministry of Justice protested, and then Colonel Simic quite laconically said: "Well, yes, but only if I approve of it. It's possible with my approval." He said something to that effect. I was there, I listened to this conversation so I was aware of the details involved in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What kind of conclusion were you able to reach, because after all you were present there all the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a flagrant violation of an order issued by the president of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could we have a number for this document, for this order of military administration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D127/1 and D127/1 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to discuss with this witness Exhibit D102/1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, tell us, please, this decree consists of two pages and it was published in issue number 12 of the Official Gazette. In practical terms, how did it function?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of this instruction published in the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska. However, as regards this instruction of the department of the Ministry of Defence and me as the head of this department, we did not have any specific task, any specific functions in terms of implementation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know which body, which particular organ, was more closely involved in the implementation of this instruction?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat for Agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There is one --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to do some clarification of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't said actually the Secretariat for Agriculture. Maybe the witness could repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript says the Secretariat for Agriculture. Which one did you mention?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned the municipal Secretariat for Economy, not Agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have now our document under the number R38? This is a handwritten document, no date, no author.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document consists of three pages. Take a look at them, please. Tell me, first of all, whether you have seen this document at all?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have. I saw it together with a number of other documents in relation which I mentioned Mr. Savic, Mr. Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What did you hear in connection with this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, who was involved with the police in the process -- in processing of persons who were found in possession of legal -- illegal documents, involving weapons, showed me a number of documents and he said that there were proceedings going on, police proceedings, that is, an investigation going on, in respect of several such offenders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have a look at page 3, the underlined portion of the text, which you will find in the middle of the page, where it says that it is necessary to organise hunters with their personal weapons during the initial stage. Was it customary for hunters to be a component part of a military organisation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The last passage on page 3, how do you interpret this? What does it mean, the establishment of "our" party documentation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law on the military does not recognise party formations, any party affiliations. They only recognise the category of military conscripts. So here the issue is -- concerns the establishment of a military unit consisting of people who were members of a specific political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have a look at page 2, somewhere in the middle of the page. There is another portion of underlined text which begins with the words, "In that sense." When you read -- analysed previously other documents, when examined them, in light of that, can you explain to us what this means, that individuals for sabotage activity should be trained? How do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With your permission, I should like to say that this document preceded the documents that we have already discussed here. Block schematic documents, where mention is made of the municipal staff and other units and then the document which we discussed at the beginning of the hearing today, which specifies in detail the military structure of this unit, together with lower ranking units, the reconnaissance platoon, the signals platoon, an observation platoon and so on and so forth. Now, if you're asking me about the meaning of this portion of the text, I can tell you that it was necessary to train personnel for sabotage activity, that is the planting of explosive devices, liquidation of persons and so on and so forth. Everything that is part of the usual activity of a sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you ever learn who the author of the document was, which body, which organisation, or which individual, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is linked to Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I would ask you to disregard that evidence unless some sort of proper foundation for the authorship of the document is made. "Linked to Alija Fitozovic" doesn't mean anything much. Furthermore, the witness hasn't really established how he recognises this document or the history of this document or indeed anything that gives you any clue as to its authenticity. He said something about it being linked or -- to Milos Savic, I think. We don't know where he saw it, when he saw it, under what circumstances he saw it or anything else that will assist you to make any sort of judgement about its authenticity. That should be dealt with if Mr. Pantelic proposes to tender the document into evidence, and furthermore, Mr. Pantelic -- he may well go on to do this, I don't know, but he shouldn't leave the evidence at -- where it merely says that the document is linked to Alija Fitozovic. Further explanation of that is needed as well. It might be my fault because I stood up at that point, but I think at this stage, further authenticity or explanation of the origins of this document is required for you to make any use of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, Your Honour, this witness clearly explained that his personal knowledge with regard to this document came from the information of the police inspector, Mr. Milos Savic, who told him that the certain ongoing investigations are conducted at that time against certain people, certain persons. So he said that. You can find it in transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that has been said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a couple of minutes ago. Secondly, this witness just testified that a link between Mr. Alija Fitozovic and this document were also mentioned at that particular time, when he spoke with the police officer, Mr. Savic. So I don't know what else -- of course we are very mindful, Your Honour, in order to absolutely establish the relevance, since Mr. Alija Fitozovic, before this honourable Trial Chamber testified here and he actually said that certain documents he made by himself were his signatures and his handwritings, then probably Defence will check this part of transcript and then in certain moment handwriting expert will give his professional opinion with regard to the document already confirmed by Mr. Alija Fitozovic before this Trial Chamber, and this particular document. So up to now, I don't see what else I can explore or ask from this witness with regard to this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that means that -- that's all the witness knows. He can't give us any further evidence as to the connection of this document to anybody, in fact, so it cannot be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ah, he personally said -- well, Your Honour, we could always discuss about the part who the author was, maybe we could have at this stage just marked as ID so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can mark it for identification purposes only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. I just wonder, Mr. Ninkovic, when you saw these pages with Mr. Savic, did you see only pages 50 and the two pages that follow, or did you see the whole document? Because the first page is marked 50, which seems to imply there were 49 pages and maybe a title page in front of it. Or were there just the three pages that we have in front of us and the 50 means nothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- the way I understood it, this was not a part of the document, so the number 50 doesn't actually mean anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the identification number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
