utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D128/1 ID and D128/1 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I would like to discuss the document D008, Defence document dated 16 of July, 1992. This is a list of fire brigade, pay list for June, 1992. Just very briefly. And also in order to speed up things, if you allow me, maybe we could have D012 because it's payroll for month of July so we could deal with that easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are not getting any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are still not getting translation. I'm wondering what's up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is a problem with the sound, Judge Mumba. We are not hearing anything here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem. The interpreters say they can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear people speaking from this microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Now I can hear, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the sound is back now, can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just put the other document on the side because they are quite similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my question to you, Mr. Ninkovic, was these are simple documents. One was is the June payroll and the other for July of that same year, 1992. What I would like to know is whether people who were members of the fireman unit in Samac, were they also under the labour obligation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were under the labour obligation. The firemen unit is of particular importance. It is a vital service in the sense of the protection of citizens and their property from fires. So we cared deeply about this service in the municipality of Samac and I personally, as the head of the department, these men on the list were organised in shifts round the clock, and they always went out to help regardless of the time of day and circumstances under which the intervention was required. I can tell you that this list includes members of all three ethnic groups. Here under number 1, we have Slobodan Milovanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You don't have to go into all that detail.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. He is an engineer, highly skilled, for this kind of work. Then we have two Croats under 2 and 8. And another Serb under 10. And all the others, that is the majority, are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell us, were these people in Samac for the duration of the war?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, could we please have a number, these two numbers for these two documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the numbers, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I thought that one of the documents just being presented now -- I apologise. There has been a mix-up with the Prosecution. It's my fault, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: First is pay list for fire brigade for month of June, 1992, and the second is for month of July.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be Exhibits D129/1 and D129/1 ter for the B/C/S and D130/1 and D130/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we be specific as to which month is which number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The list of firefighters for the month of June, 1992 is D129/1 and ter, and the list of workers in the fire company that worked in July is D130/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have now our internal number document with internal number D0013, please? This is a letter sent to the ministry section, Defence Ministry section, Samac, sent by the Secretariat for Housing, dated 16 of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, since this is addressed to your department in the ministry, just a brief explanation. I see that the Secretary of the Secretariat, Mr. Blagojevic, is asking for some persons who have already been assigned to various army units. Is this the common procedure, the one that you explained before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. I am familiar with this document and this is the common procedure which I spoke about repeatedly during the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number for this document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D131/1 and ter, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And next documents that I would like to discuss with this witness are D0015 and D0016. These are two records made by a water and sewage company, Bosanski Samac, dated 24 of September, 1992, regarding the event related to the aerial bombing of water works.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] See the dates are the same except that the record of the damage is different. What do you know about it? I don't really know whether you can tell us anything about the document, whether you are familiar with it but if not, can you tell us -- do you know anything about the incident mentioned in this record?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of this incident. I personally visited the site of the attack after the planes had flown over, after the plane had flown over. It had arrived from the direction of Croatia and flew over the mouth of the Bosna into the Sava River, which is northwest, if you look at the position of Samac. It attacked the town with explosive devices. Several civilian structures were damaged, but the particular target of the attack was the water mains, that is where water is used, the chief reservoir, the chief place from which water is distributed through the mains all over the town, and considerable material damage was inflicted on that structure. What was difficult to redress is the chlorinating installations were damaged; that is, water which comes from the ground are replete with bacteria, and therefore, you have to treat the water. It is well-known technology used to protect the population from the bacteria in the water. So water is chlorinated and the town did not have any water for a while, for several days, and it was impossible to chlorinate water for an even longer period of time, I'd say for as much as ten days, and there were cases of dysentery. That is, people came to the health centre to seek help due to the intake of polluted water.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have numbers for these documents, please, exhibit numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I take a neutral position on the admission of this document. I raise once again for the purpose -- for your assistance, whether or not you want this document to go into evidence. I simply can't see the relevance of it to any issue at all. There has never been any challenge that there was a war, that things were damaged, there were fighters and bombs coming from Croatia, so one is left scratching one's head to figure out the relevance of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the relevance could be the conditions under which the prisoners were kept, they had no water to bathe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Especially regarding the whole population, Your Honour. It is not just usual document. Our attention was -- Defence attention was with regard to the quality of water regarding of all population of Samac. So on the one side we would like to show how -- what are the efforts of the public company were to reinstall the -- and the permanent attacks on Samac contrary to the international humanitarian law, from the Croatian part of course and consequences on the whole population regardless of their ethnic background in Samac during this period of time and certain events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: As I said I remain neutral in the matter. If it's any assistance to Mr. Pantelic, the Prosecution is not adopting a position that there was no war and conditions were bad. If that's of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There are fair wars and unfair wars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the numbers, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The record listing a number of 8 damages in the first paragraph shall be Exhibit D132/1 and ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, maybe we can differentiate them by saying the one discussing damage to motor vehicles and then the other one is dealing with water works.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is fine. The one dealing with motor vehicles will be D132/1 and ter, and the second document will be Exhibit D133/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, sorry. The next document, it's our internal number D0021. These are various decisions on assignment to work obligation, mostly more of the -- let me check. Dated practically all of them are dated 28th of January, 1993. Yes, for the company Master.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly only, Mr. Ninkovic, you've already testified about the mechanism used by a certain company, institution, or military unit to request through some administrative agency, through the department of the Ministry of Defence, certain persons to work for it. Now, look at these -- look at these. Let's go quickly through this. I shall ask you briefly. First document, surname Mitrovic, what ethnicity is he?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next one, Milos Miljic. What is his ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then Pero Pejic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Nikola Pupcevic is next?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next, Mitar Popovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next, Milivoje Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next person, Edina Hadziabdic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what was her role there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was the head of the accounting department. It is second in the ranking order to the manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next, Tomislav Zarak?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next, Nedjo Vujanovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Mujanovic"]?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next, Vaso Tanasic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dragolub Stefanovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I can't hear you, Mr. Lazarevic. Your microphone was not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, maybe Mr. Pantelic could go a little bit slower because really receiving some strange names here in the transcript. Line 25 on page 50 I think it will be -- somebody Mujanovic, Serb, has no meaning for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe that it will be rectified after the checking of the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We reached Dragolub Stefanovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He is a coordinator. What did this mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Director.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Naser Seljakovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next, Zlatko Smajic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next person is Zilha Muresevic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Right. In any event, these decisions were issued practically, this was the obligation which bound all the inhabitants regardless of their ethnic origin, is it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since we are discussing the subject, did -- your wife was also under labour obligation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My wife was in Hranaprodukt. She was with commercial department. My father worked at Master, the that company we are talking about now. He was engaged in security matters. He was born in 1935.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he a janitor or what?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And my mother was representative on the agent for civil defence. She was born in 1937. I don't have a brother. And my wife's father, my wife's brother, their relatives, were either in the army or under labour obligation. I can give you their names, if necessary. And if that is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic with respect to the family members you mentioned, the jobs they were doing as part of the war work obligation, were those jobs the same jobs that they were doing before April 17th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were such cases too, but there were those who were assigned to new jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you understand the question asked by Her Honour Judge Williams well? She asked you about members of your family, not the population in general. Did you get that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain it one by one. My wife was studying agriculture in Osijek at the moment when the war broke out, and she then had to flee Osijek. She returned home. She was reading her third year, and she was put under labour obligation in Hranaprodukt.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So let's move on slightly quicker. She did not hold that job prior to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did your father hold the same job prior to April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but my mother, yes, she was assigned to the civil defence before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D134/1 and D134/1 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is Your Honour -- Your Honours, is that the whole bundle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: These assignments, assignments on work obligation, is that the whole bundle?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because they are --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: They are individual documents and individual names. I'm not -- I'm just curious to know how we are going to arrange it, that's all. I've not got any complaint about that. But I wonder if the Chamber would prefer to give it subgroupings like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Like A, B, C, D?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, something like that. It's unlikely to arise, but at some stage in the future, it might be important to know which particular document we are referring to in this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe it will be much clearer if we have A, B, C, D, according to the pages, according to the names of the particular assignees. For instance, according to the bundle that I have, the first one is Jovan Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If we can have that as A?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The second one is Milos Miljic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: B. Pero Pejic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: C. Nikola Pupcevic, D. Mitar Popovic, E. Milivoje Stefanovic, F.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I have to -- the next one is again Milivoje Stevanovic. Maybe it's a mistake. It will be at the same number. Yeah. It was a mistake, okay. The next one is Edina Hadziabdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That will be what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That would be G, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: G, yes. Tomislav Zarak, H. Nedjo Vujanovic, I. Vaso Tanasic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: J?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, J. Dragolub Stefanovic, K. Naser Seljakovic, L. Zlatko Smajic, M. And Zilha Muresevic, M.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And our next document is D0023. This is a decision on assigning housing premises dated 28th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a pretty poor copy, but I hope you will recognise it. Is it your signature in the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I see the preamble says that it deals with decrees and other regulations, isn't it? So tell us, briefly, only, is this also a disposition which has to do with the decree on the requisition of immovable -- of moveable property for the -- for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And here we are dealing with a specific institution and this is education, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the elementary school in Samac had been put on fire in the early days of the war and thus no instruction could take place there. The principal, the school's principal, analysed the problem and together with the relevant secretariat, that is the secretariat for education, in the assembly of the municipality of Samac, they decided to ask the ministry to take for these purposes the building indicated in this document, as it was thought that instruction could be provided in it even though this is not a building which can provide all the necessary conditions. But on the ground floor of this building, there was a tavern which could be refurbished more or less and make it into a makeshift classroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D135/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next document is D0024, please. This is some -- it's a letter signed by this witness, dated 29th of October, 1993, sent to the Secretariat, municipal Secretariat for Housing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another document which you signed. Tell us what is this about?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document that I signed. We can say that it means care for property. The young lady mentioned in the text, Dragica Skuljevic was with the military medical service, of the 3rd Battalion in Orlovac. Whilst there she was using a school flat. Then she was posted to a different unit, part of the 2nd Bosanska Brigade, so this flat was vacated. And this is a letter which informs the school principal and the municipal authority responsible for housing to take care of that particular apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please, for this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D136/1 and ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now I would like to discuss document RH35. It's a letter dated 25th of September, 1992, sent by secretary -- municipal Secretariat for Economy to the person who is coordinator for the work units, working units. It's an order, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, on the left-hand side, it says, "Sent to the Ministry of Defence in Bosanski Samac." This is handwritten. Tell me, what is this all about?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this document. I got it from the Secretariat for Economy. This is a government agency that saw how many people were necessary for which particular job. In this case they requested from the coordinator of the work unit to increase the number of persons who would, from time to time, carry out certain work assignments. It is also requested that in cooperation with the body that I headed, we should see whether there are any people who are able-bodied and who have no obligations although the war was still on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D137/1 and ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, how come that the stamps on the original letter and the translation are quite different?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: What's the stamp in the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The stamp in translation is actually a certificate, it's like a notary public who certifies that the translation is true and accurate so they are not related.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: To each other?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, just one matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you hear me now? I'm sorry. Just a very minor matter. The document says at the top, "SAP, Semberija and Mijovica." I assume that's a mistake and that should be SAO so that we are all clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct. It's maybe an error in typing, yes. Thank you. I'm grateful for your assistance. Next document is RH37, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is yet another document from your department. You signed it. What is this all about? What was the point of this letter?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document that I signed. This is a letter to the administration for public revenue. This agency had to pass a decree on job descriptions for the number of persons employed in that agency, also stating the specific jobs involved and the qualifications required for each and every job. Without this document, I, as head of the department, could not accept to have people assigned there. It can be seen from this document that I gave them a deadline for adopting such a document, and it is only after that that I accepted requests for persons to be assigned to work at the public revenue agency. So this was in keeping with the law and this was the way it should be done, through official channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: A number for this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. It will be Exhibit D138/1 and D138/1 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, now we have, in fact, two documents. The first is RH40 and the second is RH41. In fact, this is practically a cover from the book of General Martin Spegelj, titled Reminiscences of a Soldier. And the second document is an extract, a map, from the -- depicted from this book, and it's related to the military and political situation in Croatia from December, 1991, until the -- January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm interested in the following. Please look at the map in the corner. First of all, tell me, did you read this book?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this map, this map here on the other page, I would like to hear your comment regarding this particular little arrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We are trying to find the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's RH41.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm interested in the following, bearing in mind your knowledge from the field of military matters. This little arrow, number 8, what does it actually denote? I must say that regrettably, due to the quality of the copy, in the legend this number 8 cannot be seen, because if I remember correctly, in the original in the book, it is in red. Perhaps that's why it didn't come out in this photocopy, but we are going to try to provide the Trial Chamber will colour copies of this map. Regrettably, it's only now that I notice this. But you please tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, if you know, of course, how do you interpret this arrow with number 8 on it, on this map? What is your personal and professional knowledge in this regard?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This arrow is the planned thrust of the attack of the Army of the Republic of Croatia against Bosnia-Herzegovina, along the line between Slavonski Brod and Bosanski Brod, and then further on towards the south. This is a strategic plan. And now I'll tell you why. Those who are familiar with the geography of Bosnia-Herzegovina know the following: Bosanski Brod, Doboj, Zenica, Sarajevo, Mostar, the Adriatic Sea, that is a strategic direction, all of that, where the main roads and railroads are, the main communications. Then also the valleys of the Bosna and Neretva rivers. That is where the main potentials are, that is to say urban areas, industry, et cetera. This strategic line, direction, divides Bosnia-Herzegovina into two parts, which is to say that whoever takes that line will dominate, strategically and militarily, over Bosnia-Herzegovina. I know personally that only in a small part, along this -- only along a small line along this part, Podnovlje is a place 20 kilometres away from Doboj, and then all the way to Doboj, only that part was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. And the rest, that is to say all the way from the Sava River to the Adriatic Sea was under the control of the Croat forces, that is to say of the regular Croatian Army, the Croatian Defence Council, and the Muslim Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a question in conclusion: The territory of the municipality of Samac, was that within this planned, strategic direction of the attack of the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have exhibit numbers for these two document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The cover from the book will be Exhibit D139/1 and ter for the B/C/S. And the extract of the map from the book will be Exhibit D140/1 and ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now a document under [Microphone not activated] --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Could we now have document under our internal number RB9? This is a request signed by this witness, Mr. Ninkovic, dated 6th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that it is you who signed this letter, Mr. Ninkovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify something. It's not quite clear. On -- it says here that this is sent to the executive board of Samac and military code 7445. Are these one address or two?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Two different addresses. The executive committee is -- council is the government of Samac, whereas military post code 7445 is the public name of a military unit. A military unit has its military name and this other name. So this is the 2nd Posavina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So this is practically addressed to two addresses?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who were copies provided to? That's what it says on the document itself and that only confirms your thesis, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please remember to pause. The interpreters are under pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, what was the pretext, or rather, what was the reason why this letter was sent?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, human resources are of particular importance in war, and the rational use of human resources is a precondition for successful warfare. The Ministry of Defence assigned the personnel available within the military. They were assigned to work duty and to other structures. Human potentials, resources, are spent during the war. That is to say people get killed, are wounded, but also some flee from the area involved. So every structure required more personnel in order to successfully carry out all its assignments. Specifically, the military asked for more military conscripts, for having more military conscripts, mobilised, and the executive council, the civilian authorities, requested more people for work obligation so that they could manufacture material goods that are indeed spent to a great extent in the war. So there was tension between the two. The ministry was between, so to speak, the military and the civilian structures. It was very difficult to satisfy everyone, because there weren't enough personnel. So the motive, why I wrote this letter, was for the executive council to see whether all job descriptions were justified, whether indeed so many personnel were required in companies and institutions, and perhaps whether some military conscripts who were given work obligation could be replaced by women, that is to say personnel who are not military conscripts, whereas those who are military conscripts and who are doing their work obligation could be assigned to the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's just try to be as efficient as possible. The last sentence that says, "Bringing citizens in by the military police," could you please comment upon that particular sentence? What was the reason? What led your Ministry of Defence to react to this case of the military police bringing in certain citizens?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, this was the order issued by the commander of the military unit, for the military police to go to a company and to arrest military conscripts and send them to the front line, which is illegal, of course. I, as an official of the Ministry of Defence, opposed this because this is an attack against the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, work obligation also is a type of war assignment. So --

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You explained that before.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the commander of the military unit does not have the right to change anybody's war assignment. He is not in a position to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please, for this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D141/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now we could discuss all three remaining documents, RB12, RB13 and RB14. In fact, these are three decisions of the work obligation dated, first one is 11 of February, second one also 11 of February, and third one is 18 of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is what we discussed earlier on, right? These are also the forms that you explained. The first two documents for Mr. Drago Sego, who was a cashier, and the other one for Huseinagic Majda, she was a financial bookkeeper, in the middle of these forms, it says that the Ministry of Defence agrees, that they give their approval. So I imagine that that is one of the forms that these departments took?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is the following: The third document, dated the 18th of May, 1993, it has a different type of form. Can you explain briefly what the reason for that was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the preamble of the first two documents, and then if you look at the third one, you can see that the regulations involved were changed, but the regulations pertained to the same area. The other regulation also said that it was only the head of the department that can sign a decision to assign a person to work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have numbers for these three documents?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The three decisions, in the order in which they were given, they will be Exhibits D142/1 and ter, D143/1 and ter, and D144/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question. Mr. Drago Sego, he is ethnically what?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I just -- just so that we don't get confused later on, I understand there was -- the documents were given their numbers according to the order in which they were introduced. There is a bit of confusion on our part as to the order in which they were confused (sic). We just want to be clear which one is which. So if we could just clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will clarify that. First exhibit is D142/1. It's with the name of Sego, Drago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is his ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Sego is an ethnic Croat. He lives in Samac now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did he live in Samac during the war as well?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Second document is 143/1, name Huseinagic Majda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This lady, what is her ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is she still in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The third document, [In English] 144/1, the name of Hajric Amir, [Interpretation] what is his ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he still lives in Samac or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now I would like to discuss some Prosecution exhibits with this witness. Could we have Exhibit P3, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, please take a look at this document. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw it only while undergoing preparations with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before we discussed this, before this case, did you -- had you ever seen this document before that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher, thank you. Could we now have Exhibit P18, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, could you please put this on the ELMO so that the other participants in these proceedings can see this? Please take a look at the other sheets of paper as well. My question is the following. On the bottom of the left-hand -- on the left, is the date of the 10th of March. That is quite clear to everyone, isn't it? The 10th of March, 1992, in Donji Hasic. Did you personally have any knowledge about the activities related to the procurement of weapons, collecting funds for these purposes, before April, 1992, in the territory of the municipality of Samac? And if so, what was your knowledge in this respect?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my office there was a man called Ivica Ivkic, who also worked there. He was a MP in the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He was a MP from the Croat Defence Council. I was a member of the Liberal Party. We talked about the situation on the eve of the war. He mentioned to me that within the Croatian Defence Union -- Croatian -- the HDZ, that money was being collected for procuring weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we now have exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, is that evidence somehow linked to this document? If it is, perhaps the witness had better take -- explain that to us or perhaps Mr. Pantelic could ask the witness how it's related to this document. The document is shown, then the witness gives evidence about general arming of the Croat population. Now, the document must have been shown for a reason and if the witness has got something further that he can add about this document, this exhibit, then of course I have no objection. But what's occurring is the document is placed in front of the witness and then he talks about general arming as if there is a connection between the two. So if there is a connection, let's hear it. He may know something about what happened or may know something about the people or this episode or something about the document. But the way it comes out, it's as if the witness is talking about this particular document and you look again and it seems that it's just general talk and that's what I am concerned to avoid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Well, I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, since this is the local commune of Donji Hasici, did you have any knowledge about this? It was my understanding that you were speaking about the municipality of Bosanski Samac before April, 1992, but specifically did you have any personal knowledge about the local communes in the territory of Bosanski Samac before April, 1992, in which there were certain activities that you referred to, those related to arming and, if you could give us some names and how you found out about this, what your sources were?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ivica Ivkic lived in Hrvatska Tisina. Hasic, Gornji and Donji Hasic are in the immediate neighbourhood. He protested against some Croats who were employed abroad and who did not want to give their contributions for procuring weapons, and he pointed out that there were others who did give money for that, and they had a cashier there and money was collected for these purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it time for our break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will continue the proceedings in the afternoon at 14.30 hours in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because we were informed that we were going to withdraw -- okay. Thank you, Your Honour. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you're continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have finished with these documents. Let us discuss something in connection with this working unit and some exhibits of the Prosecution, P37. You see this document here. You have already spoken about similar issues. Have you seen this document already? Can you comment on it, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a payroll for the members of the work obligation unit, but what I should perhaps add by way of clarification is the following: That the number of days and the months, April, May, June, July and August, five times 30, 150, minus 20, because not all of the April is included, then we can speak about the total of 130 days, as we can see, none of these people had 130 active days, days of service. It means that the remainder of the time they were at home and doing their usual work, which confirms the fact that the decree was implemented in such a way that these works were of a temporary nature. These people were called whenever there was work to do. The difference in the total number of days depends on individual qualifications of these people and what kind of needs were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If you would excuse me, I would intervene and ask whether this list we had on the screen just some seconds ago, was it as to ethnicity, a mixed list? So there were Serbs, Muslims and Croats? Can the witness ask -- answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe he should be shown the list again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think they are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One additional question, please. How do you explain the word "additional" payroll? What does this word "additional" mean? Do you have any knowledge as to the reasons why it was added to the title?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means maybe additional amount of money, maybe they were given some more money.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information whether this work unit in Samac in 1992 between April and August, did it consist of only 11 people or was it larger?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period of time I was not involved in this type of work. I have already explained this in my testimony but I believe that it was larger.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In this context, and in view of what you just said, that it was probably larger than this, how would you explain the word dodatan, that is additional, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe it was the additional sum of money that was given to them. Maybe they had already received a certain amount of money and then they were given some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's not probably that important, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It may be important. That's twice the witness has speculated that additional means extra money, supplementary in the English translation. I would ask that you ignore that evidence unless Mr. Pantelic can lead this witness to something more concrete, establishing that it's -- means more money. Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it does show from his answers that he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He doesn't know, no. I perhaps just highlight that point, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have an additional question. Is this perhaps -- this is some kind of speculation from my side -- a formal document, or do you have any evidence of that -- that this money was really paid to these persons, in one form or another?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, you have heard the question of His Honour Judge Lindholm. Who was in charge to ensure the payment for the people engaged in the work obligation unit? This is just one aspect of the problem. This concerns only this work unit.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who requested engagement of work obligation units for their needs were required to pay these people. If it was the executive council, then they would supposed to pay for it. Here in the signature I see that this is the President of the executive council. It was so it was preferably the executive council which initially requested the engagement of these people, so they must have paid them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As far as public companies in the municipality are concerned, how was the money insured? From what sources I'm not referring to individuals but public companies such as water works, public utility companies, power distribution companies and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the municipal or public companies, and institutions, and the money is provided from the municipal budget, and there are relevant decisions for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So practically speaking if I understand you correctly, it was the municipality that had to ensure the resources necessary for the work obligation for the public companies in the territory of the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have now please, Exhibit P38? It's already -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have spoken several times about the people who were either killed or wounded. Since this document was created on the 17th of November, 1992, it comes from the President of the executive council, as far as I can see, what can you tell us about it? You have already mentioned fatalities and casualties. Do you know how their families were compensated and do you know the circumstances under which the individuals on this list --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The phrasing of that question is unfortunate. It assumes and is a clear and unequivocal signal to this witness that there was compensation paid to these people. It's just -- the assumption is clear. Do you know how compensation was paid to the families. We don't know that that occurred at all. That has to be established first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm referring to the document by itself, my dear friend. You see in the left, bottom-hand corner there is some, I would say, information with regard to the payment of the family member. So we have that on the list. And I'm going to discuss that, what does it mean with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's fine. I've got no problem with that. I'm happy for the witness to be led to the notations on the dot. I'm not trying to stop that. Mr. Pantelic is perfectly within his rights to do that, but his question presupposed the existence of compensation. That's what I read in the transcript and that's what I'm concerned about. I don't want the witness being -- that notion being put into his mouth by Mr. Pantelic. That's all I'm concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, I think the intervention is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's find out what the witness's personal knowledge is about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, tell me first of all whether you are aware of the fact that these people were killed. Is this the number that you spoke about? Was the number perhaps higher, the number of the killed and the wounded? We addressed the issue a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about these fatalities, about the people that were killed. It's difficult for me to say whether these are the individuals who were killed, but some of the persons on the list were known to me. I heard about their death subsequently, later on. I cannot tell you exactly what the circumstances of their death were. This can be described only by eye witnesses, the people who happened to be in the vicinity of those who got killed. If we are talking about the killing or wounded of certain persons, then adequate records should be found, with the military administration. If these people were killed while carrying out duties for the needs, for the military, then appropriate records should be found with the military. I don't think that it is contested that this payment was indeed made. The issue was discussed several times, on several occasions, at the executive council and I'm sure that a document to that -- in that -- to that effect should be found somewhere in the files of the finance department.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So why was this payroll made? It's clear that this is a payroll. Do you have any personal knowledge about the reasons for drafting this payroll?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would have been pointless to have a payroll done if no payments were to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is this your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The point, witness, is that you don't know whether any payment was actually made.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mean I cannot provide any documents to support this -- the fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned the fact that you knew that a number of people were conducting proceedings against Republika Srpska for damages. Do you remember who these individuals are? Who are the people who are conducting these proceedings for compensation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. I'm interested in the name. Who is the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you told us that you knew a person who was involved in such proceedings against the state. Do you remember -- do you happen to remember his name?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Goran Kljajic. He used to work at the memorial centre in Samac. He's a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And he was the one who took the state to court for compensation because he -- he had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, against the -- against Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, I'm a little bit confused. The gentleman that Mr. Ninkovic mentions takes the state to court for compensation because he was has been wounded. Was this man doing work obligation at the time and if so, what type of work obligation? Because this morning, we heard about people going to court for compensation with respect to property and so on and so forth, but maybe we could just have a bit more clarity on this particular point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that proceedings are being conducted before a court, a court of law, but I am not familiar with the circumstances of his wounding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us try to clarify. Goran Kljajic was wounded during the war, was he not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This is mightily leading. It's being handed on a plate to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to summarise, Your Honour, the statement of this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's clear he has said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He said that Goran Kljajic is a Croat and he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And he has said he was not familiar with the circumstances of his wounding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have any knowledge whether he was a member of a work unit or was he involved in some other work obligation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the fact that he was wounded. That's one thing. But as I told you, I don't know the circumstances of his wounding. What else did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of a work unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have, please, Exhibit P39?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this payroll, we see a certain number of persons who were in charge of where various types of work for work brigades. These nine individuals here, they were employees of which particular service, which secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This service was in charge of the work obligation units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But they were part of which institution? Who paid the salaries?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were independent, but the salaries were provided by the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were these individuals also employees of the Defence Ministry?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the coordinator was? Because here we see that there were some officers in charge, but we do not see who their supervisor was.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzevad Celic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is his ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit P49, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, have you ever seen this document? Did you see it at the time it was created in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since it covers the area that you addressed in your testimony this morning, what comment could you give it? What professional comment you can give to this particular document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last paragraph, we read the following sentence -- I mean a sentence that deals with the issue of compensation, and the damages to be paid at the end of the war. So it contains provisions pertaining to the material obligation, pertaining to the financial obligation. However, I don't think this is the signature of the person -- I mean it's not illegible -- a legible signature, and I don't think it is the signature of Dr. Blagoje Simic, whose signature I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me whether this was the usual form of such orders at the time you established your department, the Defence Ministry department, and which body had the authority to issue this type of order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This type of document could be created by the National Defence Ministry or the Secretariat for National Defence, but in view of the date, the 27th of June, this was a transitional period when the National Defence Secretariat had ceased to work and the military -- and the department of the Ministry of Defence was not yet created. I think Milivojevic [As interpreted] was relieved of his duty on the 13th or 14th of June and I was appointed the chief of the department on the 16th of July, so this was a transitional period and they were not able to conduct this type of work at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The record needs to be corrected on page 79 line 3. You mentioned Mr. Milos Bogdanovic and not Mr. Milivojevic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just to set the record straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, just to assist Mr. Pantelic, it seems that he hasn't got an answer to part of his question. He asked the witness whether this document was the usual form of such orders and the witness went on to provide an explanation, but as far as I can see, did not tell us whether this was the usual form for such requisitions or call it whatever you will and it's important for the Prosecution to know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness answer that part of the question, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two documents were in use, two documents that were accurate. One was called "decision on mobilisation." It was an administrative type of document whereby it was possible to requisition certain material. And there was another type of form that could also be used, which, during the former SFRY, had been printed, and it provided for the possibility of the commander of the relevant military unit to requisition specified property when necessary. When the organ of administration was not accessible, depending on how far they were located, how far from the town, then in that case, he was the one who could issue the mobilisation call-up, which consisted of three parts, the disposition and the delivery form, the delivery note. But this document has, elements of a decision. However, a more appropriate term would be a decision and not an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit P65.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the counsel would switch on his microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's ID. Is it ID? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It is a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is an exhibit, Mr. Pantelic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Checking here. Yes. Could we -- could the exhibit be shown to the witness? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is very -- this is a document which is barely legible but try, if you can, tell us what it is about. If you can't...

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is barely legible and the second sentence I simply can't make it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you recall it, as this is the municipal Secretariat for National Defence and I see the seal so it must be the time prior to mid-April, that is before the conflict broke out in Samac, so I thought because since you worked in the Secretariat that perhaps you might have some recollection of this. If not, then never mind.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is an application that part of the Sitex company, I mean the premises, be requisitioned or placed at the disposal of the Yugoslav People's Army. And it is a properly formed, worded document. Although there should be something else too if this was carried through.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is what I was going to ask you. Did the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, prior to mid-April, 1992, I mean the authorities responsible for the defence, did they apply the same methodology as we could see in that decree on the use of the moveable property during the war that we discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the layout is identical in the former SFRY and the new law, the new defence law of the Republika Srpska, and all the laws which derived from it, except that the new law has been cleaned up of the clutter and is smaller and it does not include certain things that existed in the former defence law of SFRY.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are sorry but the counsel was speaking over the witness and we could not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, please remember to wait for the witness to complete his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. My question was the following. I do apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, my question is not in. These matters concerning the use of real estate by the army, if need be, was this principle also applied in the other Bosnia-Herzegovinian entity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the technology, the mobilisation, what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What you have just been explaining to us?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The procedure is the same. The laws were the same. I mean those which were in effect in the Serb entity and the Croat-Muslim entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit P67, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the light of the date, which this document bears, and that is the 13th of April, 1992, tell me, since at that time you were in the municipal Secretariat for National Defence, so will you please explain to us what is the town command? What kind of institution is it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Law does not know that term. Town command is a term which was not specified by law. So this is a new notion as a notion. And the rest I can comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. Wait, I'll ask you a question. On the 13th of April, 1992, was there such a thing as town command in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only lawful armed formation was the Yugoslav People's Army, and it did not embrace such an institution, such an agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please, will you clear a certain situation up for me? I understand what the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence is, but I understand that the town command, I don't know, some town command, will you please read it, and then comment on what kind of knowledge do you have about this situation, that is described in this document -- in this letter.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that it means that the paramilitary body, which calls itself the town command, voices its readiness to -- that the paramilitary-- to place paramilitary formations under the control of the municipal TO staff. At the same time, the municipal TO staff had no jurisdiction over the armed forces. The Territorial Defence made an integral part of the armed forces. There was this integral system made of the Yugoslav People's Army and the Territorial Defence. Therefore, this -- the addressee here is wrong; that is, it comes from a body which does not exist by statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now look down at the seal. Is it common for political parties to play a role in matters of this nature?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already testified repeatedly about this. This is a clear, most blatant incursion of political parties in the defence system. The law is familiar with this and this is liable for Prosecution, that is, the police and courts and everybody else. That is, charges may be brought against whoever sets up a paramilitary body and arms people unlawfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I wonder whether my colleague, Mr. Di Fazio, because your mike was on so maybe -- I thought maybe you had some --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I was going to raise a matter but I declined to do so. I'll raise it in cross-examination, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P75, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two, two pages, this document has two pages. Now, have a look at them and tell us what you know about this document, if that is, you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing special about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could we have Exhibit P76, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what do you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm privy to its contents. You see the JNA used the ordinary olive-green/grey uniforms and this was the time of June when in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina in that part of the Balkans, we have very lush vegetation. So that camouflage uniforms are much better, as they are less conspicuous; that is, the soldier wearing them is less conspicuous. And because of that, an army unit asked the civilian authorities in the Samac municipality to ask the local company called Tekstilac to make for them those camouflage, those disrupted pattern uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are all citizens and conscripts from the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll just repeat the question. So members of this special purpose battalion, where did they come from? What is their origin? What is their provenance?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are citizens of Samac, and the municipality of Samac, and those who were subject to conscription, and they were called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, if you know, how strong was that unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it varied between 150 and 250, 260 members, and this term, "Special" is inadequate because that unit had some mobile missions to perform. That is, if it happened that in some section of the front, the Serb defences were under threat, then this special, that is mobile, battalion, would go to help out, to avoid any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know who commanded that unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Josic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where does he come from?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Obudovac, municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was just go about to ask you whether this is in the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D55/1, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is self-explanatory. It's a payroll, of course, and we won't really dwell on it. Tell me, under number -- I think it's number -- could it be 11? Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you explain it for us, since it's May, 1992, can you tell me what was the role that you had on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of the Crisis Staff. I was with the public relations, with the information service, set up for the civilian authorities in the municipality of Samac. My superior was Simeon Simic. He was the head of this public relations service and I worked by and large as a journalist, that is I performed journalistic jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was it that you held that job and performed these activities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's see. Sometime between the 20th, 21st, 22nd, some -- from then, the 21st, 22nd, April, and practically until I was appointed the head of the department on the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And tell me, can you please tell us in more detail --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, before we finish with this document, Mr. Ninkovic, if, as you say, you were not a member of the Crisis Staff, on line 14, I'm just wondering if that was the case, what were you doing on a payroll entitled Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bosanski Samac? And are, as you say, number 11 on the list, "Information, pay scale number 3, coefficient 1.45, and an amount of dinars, quite a big sum, but we know there was inflation. I'm just wondering if you weren't a member of the Crisis Staff, why were you number 11 on this list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In addition, before your answer, your superior, who you say was your superior, Mr. Simeon Simic, was a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's no problem to explain this. This is a letter of the technical secretary in the Crisis Staff service. He must have put it there in a certain order, in a particular sequence, but I was not a member of the Crisis Staff and my job was to provide information and why he put me there, I do not know. Mr. Mitrovic was -- is, incidentally, a man who never had a day of work, of seniority, behind him, and took this job practically from the school desk, even though I think that this job necessitates experience and knowledge of state administration. And as far as I know, he frequently provided rather slipshod definitions of names and notions and so on and so forth. So this is merely a reflection of his ignorance of the system. And this money, this is a pitiful amount, it's just a pittance, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us try to clear this up. Please focus, Mr. Ninkovic. Look at the amount. It says 412.460 dinars. Just a moment, just a moment, easy does it. Don't tell me anything, but add up roughly this whole amount and tell us, from Blagoje Simic down, and tell us what will be the sum -- don't explain anything to me, just add it up.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under those ordinal number? 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Easy, easy. Tell me, behind your name --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So we can get through quickly, if those figures add up to 412.000, let's her hear it and let's get through it quickly rather than put the witness through some sort of arithmetic exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just roughly because obviously he's bit little confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, please does it mean that you received 412.000 and others received 40?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well this is the sum. I don't know why you're asking me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But why is it next to your name? What is the reason behind it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess an ignoramus, somebody who doesn't know how to add up things or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was that your pay that month?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There are a certain number of persons here who were involved in security, cooks and so on and so forth. Now, and which category do you belong in, if you compare these coefficients that you find in column 4? Look at it, it will be easier for you to look to your right. Now, according to that coefficient, what could you be in this body? You already said that you were a civil servant and that were you responsible for public relations?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see the difference. I have 1.45. Mr. Simic has 1.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that. Mr. Ninkovic, take it easy. Which means that you worked as what in this body?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalistic jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who was your boss?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simeon Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please describe to us the period from April, 1992, until your appointment, as you told us, whether it was June or July, 1992, what was -- will you describe to the Court what it is that you did?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my job involved information. That was to report from the territory of the municipality of Samac, for some news houses. I was especially in contact with Tanug which is the largest agency in Yugoslavia, a political newspaper and the Vecernje novosti, the newspaper. I also maintained contact with certain media houses which requested information about things -- about developments in that area. Then I was -- I also had the opportunity to receive journalists coming to the territory of the municipality of Samac, whether from the world at large or from Yugoslavia, to take them to some location, so that they can see it, to write their stories, so these are conventional jobs. I also was involved into TV stories, together with Mr. Simic, for the Belgrade Television. These stories were broadcast via satellite in Belgrade Television programmes, and I was the narrator, I helped to put together the text and I also was involved as a cameraman because our service wasn't all that developed; that is, we didn't have all the cameramen and editors and everything else. As I was an amateur cameraman; that is, I had a camera so I could take some footage.
